md: - **First ARC on Lokpal and Lokayukta:** it recommended a Lokpal at the Union (Centre) level and Lokayuktas in the States.
- **Venue of PM's projects:** PM Narendra Modi launched the projects worth about ₹17,900 crore at **Bhogapuram** (Vizianagaram district) on 1 August 2026, at the dedication of the new airport.
- **Tilaka Manjari:** a Sanskrit prose romance written by **Dhanapala**, a Jain poet at the Paramara court (Munja and Bhoja), c. 1000 CE.
- **Muziris:** the Periplus describes Muziris, on the Malabar coast (Kerala), as a port abounding with ships from Arabia and Greece.
- **Crafts:** good roads and state incentives encouraged crafts in the Mauryan period.
- **Heavy taxation:** Kosambi also points to very heavy taxes, raised even on actors and prostitutes, as a sign of the money crisis of the later Mauryas.
- **Other coins:** Kanishka's coins show the Buddha; Mahmud of Ghazni issued silver coins with Arabic and Sanskrit legends.
- **NMHC site:** The National Maritime Heritage Complex (NMHC) is being built at **Lothal**, Gujarat, the Harappan port town.
- **Upanishads = Vedanta:** the Upanishads are called **Vedanta** ("end of the Vedas") because they come at the close of Vedic literature.
- **Kusinara and Pava (Malla):** the Buddha attained **parinirvana at Kusinara**; Mahavira died at **Pava**.

- **Little lasting political effect:** Alexander stayed in India only about 19 months; his campaign left almost no lasting political mark, while the earlier Persian rule left a deeper influence on script, art and administration.
- **Errors in Indica:** besides the wrong "no slavery" claim, Indica has uncritical tales such as gold-digging ants; Strabo, following Megasthenes, wrote that Indians did not know writing.

- **Sanskrit under the later Ikshvakus:** inscriptions of later Ikshvaku kings such as Ehuvala Chamtamula at Nagarjunakonda are in Sanskrit, so Sanskrit became prominent under the Ikshvakus after their early Prakrit records.
- **Chaitika sects:** The five Chaitika sects (Purvasaila, Aparasaila, Uttarasaila, Rajagirika, Siddharthika) were branches of the **Mahasanghikas**, founded by **Mahadeva Bhikshu**.
- **Kannada Ratnatraya:** Pampa, Ponna and Ranna are called the 'three gems' (Ratnatraya) of Kannada literature.
- **Length of the conflict:** The Rashtrakuta–Vengi (Eastern Chalukya) wars went on for about 200 years.
- **Gram Sabha (Art. 243A):** Article 243A deals with the Gram Sabha, the body of all registered voters of a village Panchayat area.
- **Intermediate tier (Art. 243B):** Under the 73rd Amendment, a State whose population does not exceed 20 lakh need not set up Panchayats at the intermediate level.
- **Temple as meeting place:** Chola temples were also the venues where village assemblies held their meetings.

- **DILRMP (modern land records):** The Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme's first phase ran from 2008 to 2016; the 2016–2026 phase brought ULPIN (Bhu-Aadhaar), a unique ID for each land parcel.
- **Khajuraho:** The Khajuraho temples of the Chandelas, such as Kandariya Mahadeva, are in the Nagara style.
- **1296 raid:** Alauddin Khalji led it while he was governor of Kara under his uncle, Sultan **Jalaluddin Khalji**, before he became Sultan himself.
- **Guru Tegh Bahadur:** called **"Hind-di-Chadar"** (Shield of India); founded **Chak Nanki** (1665), which grew into Anandpur Sahib.
